subject: Week 38: build the preschool long-list — tours open in September
bodyText:
This week
Receptive language is the story of days 264 through 270: he likely understands 20 to 50 words and follows a simple command or two, while production may be one to three specific words or none at all — the CDC 2022 revision places words beyond mama and dada at the 15-month checkpoint. Cruising is fluid for many and standing alone briefly is emerging for some, both CDC 12-month checkpoints rather than requirements today. Cognitively he searches for hidden objects and uses objects the way they are meant to be used: cup to mouth, brush to hair.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Early negotiation behavior — pointing at what he wants, protesting when it does not arrive. Testing the limit is cognitive progress, not defiance.
- [low concern] A cold cycling through the house in the middle of RSV and influenza season — supportive care only; no over-the-counter cough or cold medicine under age 2.
- [monitor] No babbling, or babble without consonant variety, heading into the 12-month visit — write down examples now rather than reconstructing them later.
- [call within 24h] A cold that worsens after day five, new wheezing, or resting breathing faster than 60 breaths a minute.
- [call now] Fever ≥102F rectal with lethargy, labored breathing with retractions or nasal flaring, or blue lips or unresponsiveness — 911.

Enrichment opportunities
- Build the preschool long-list this month, then close the tab. Pull the ISSFBA directory, note the per-school application fees ($50 to $100 across eight to 10 schools), and calendar September 2027 — tour season for the fall he turns 2, with applications due that January and him at 16 to 20 months on the tours. No school takes an application under about 18 months and tour slots reset annually, so touring before roughly 14 months buys nothing. ISSFBA admission process: https://www.issfba.org/admission-process/
- Probe comprehension once a day with your hands still: say give me the ball without pointing, and watch what happens. Receptive vocabulary leads expressive by one to three months in year one, so what he understands is the better read on progress right now. CDC 1-year milestones: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
- Move hand-held walking outdoors onto uneven ground — grass, sand, a gentle slope. Varied surfaces force the ankle and hip corrections a flat hallway never asks for, and hand-held stepping is the rehearsal that runs while balance catches up. AAP: Movement 8 to 12 Months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-8-to-12-Months.aspx
- Trade one bedtime story for a single-word naming book, name each image, then stop talking for two seconds. The pause is what converts labeling into a turn he can take. AAP early literacy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/early-childhood/early-literacy/

Upcoming
- Day 252-280 (Jan 18–Feb 15, 2027): 9-month well visit — 16 days left. If it is done, close the loop on the iron rescreen and influenza #2 if this is his first flu season; if not, take any slot offered this week.
- Day 270-365 (Feb 5–May 11, 2027): preschool list-building window opens Friday — the long-list and one September calendar entry are the whole required action.
- Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first dental visit due by the first birthday — ask for the referral at the next visit and book the spring slot.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Pulls to stand at furniture or your legs
  AAP window: day 240-365
  What to look for: Time to switch to a lower crib mattress setting if not already.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/pulls-to-stand/complete

- Babbles with inflection (sounds like speech)
  AAP window: day 240-330
  What to look for: Jargon. Pitch and rhythm of a sentence without recognizable words.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/babbles-with-inflection/complete

- Explores objects by shaking, banging, throwing, dropping
  AAP window: day 240-365
  What to look for: Systematic property exploration. Repetitive drops are research, not defiance.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/explores-objects-many-ways/complete

- Lets objects go voluntarily (drops on purpose)
  AAP window: day 240-365
  What to look for: Controlled release — distinct from accidental dropping. Predecessor to throwing.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/lets-objects-go-voluntarily/complete

- Pokes with index finger
  AAP window: day 240-365
  What to look for: Isolated finger use. Predecessor to pointing.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/pokes-with-index/complete
